To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the shape of an image silhouette is a good predictor of human body pose, (2) the shape of a silhouette can be represented by a histogram-of-shape context descriptor, (3) the histogram of shape context descriptor can be used to train a regression function that recovers pose from single images, and (4) the regression function can be used in a tracker to recover pose from monocular image sequences

(1) the use of shape descriptors based on histogram of shape contexts provides good performance in recovering pose from single images; (2) the use of relevance vector machines provides a sparse and robust regressor that can handle missing data and is more robust to over-fitting than ridge regression; and (3) the use of a regressive tracking approach provides stable pose tracking over long sequences.
